open_obligations: Check the underlying evidence in Section 4.3 and Appendix G (double consultancy 75% vs debate 77%; one-turn vs two-turn accuracy)
Note that Irving et al.'s claim concerns optimal play, while these debaters are 8B models after two DPO iterations
Check whether the LLM judge's insensitivity to refutation would also hold for human judges
out.other_title: Central claim of debate: it is harder to lie than to refute a lie
out.rationale: Irving et al. propose refutation as the core reason debate should work (lies are easier to refute than to defend). The authors' evidence points the other way in their setting: double consultancy nearly matches debate, and one-turn debates are judged as accurately as two-turn ones. This challenges the mechanism, not debate's usefulness, and the authors hedge it ('does not yet seem', 'in our setting').
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether explicit refutation drives judge accuracy in debate; holds for an LLM judge in information-asymmetric reading comprehension with short debates

text: The authors recall that Irving et al. (2018) cited refutation as a key mechanism for why debate might succeed. They report finding little evidence that refutation materially affects the judge's decisions in their setting, and argue instead that debate beats consultancy because of a combination of other factors.
title: Arnesen et al. find little evidence that refutation, Irving et al.'s key mechanism, sways judges
